reviewType: read-only Forge37 channel-source and prior TCP-failure review

sourceFindings.finding: REGISTER updates FML_MC_REGISTRY ChannelList, requires NUL-terminated names, and notifies union of old/new targets. It does not fill FML_CONNECTION_DATA.
isRemotePresent only reads NetworkHooks.getConnectionData(manager).getChannels(), not the MC registry.
Forge login C2SModListReply supplies the FMLConnectionData channel map.
Raw PLAY payload dispatch is by registered local channel name and direction, independent of isRemotePresent/FMLConnectionData.
Vanilla PLAY custom payload calls NetworkHooks.onCustomPayload.
Unknown vanilla payload IDs are offered to NetworkHooks.onCustomPayload.

conclusion: Current transport.available mistakes the Forge-only login channel map for general raw-channel availability; the source predicts the observed Node timeout and also blocks standard Fabric companion reports before sending a nonce.
minimalProductionProposal: Require the existing exact live PLAY Connection/listener identity before sending the one nonce; remove the Forge-only isRemotePresent prerequisite. Keep report validation, device policy, isolation, deadlines and report bounds unchanged. Rebuild a new candidate and retest; preserve old bytes/results.
alternativeScope: A real FML login QA handshake can test Forge-to-Forge but cannot establish standard raw/Fabric interoperability. Registration-event booleans alone are unsafe as exact membership queries because events cover the old/new union without exposing the current set.
bounds: No source edit or Java run in this review.
The original runtime did not directly log FMLConnectionData; cause is established by actual pinned source and consistent failed behavior, not a fabricated attribute measurement.
Ordinary absent companions would still need to satisfy the same report requirement or time out; capability registration is not attestation.
